claims_disputed.claim: Agents reproduce omissions of their source documents, and independent human review is needed to catch them.
claims_disputed.reason: Only one source-omission incident exists (case 1, the missing defect-annihilation term, §3.1/§4.2). The case 2 incident is hallucinated digitized data, which is a different failure, not an inherited omission. §3.1 says the omission was found 'through human review and testing' and §4.2 says 'adversarial human review and extensive testing', so the paper does not isolate human review as the necessary catch. The omission also skewed the comparison against experimental data, which an automated V&V check could plausibly flag. One incident supports 'this can happen', not a general tendency or a necessity claim.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: The framework does more than mention execution checks. Table 1 makes the full V&V suite a required CI gate for every contribution; in case 1 the agent generated tests and gold files; §4.3 reports the agent running tests in case 2. That is use without an isolating comparison, so 'introduces'.

missed_issues: Fig. 1's improvement from 23.1% to 9.2% RMSPE comes from Bayesian calibration against the same TDS spectrum it is compared with, and case 2 is likewise calibrated to hand-digitized data (§3.2). These are fits, not out-of-sample validation. §3.2's sentence 'the agreement is sufficient to validate the proposed development workflow' does not follow, because a calibrated fit says nothing about the workflow.

Untagged pattern P21 clearly applies. §4.3 prescribes git pre-commit hooks that run outside the agent loop for non-negotiable provenance requirements, and makes branch protection and access controls a required part of any deployment. That is policy-as-code guardrails, though it is not evaluated.

The order of events is suggestive but anecdotal. In both cases the agent obeyed the AGENTS.md rule to request an issue number at session start (§3.1, §3.2), but it neglected documented instructions later in long sessions (§4.3). That points to start-of-session instruction files decaying over a session, which supports checkpoint or hook enforcement, but there are no counts.
§4.3 recommends 'condensing the agent's context and prompting it to critically review' at stable stages, and decomposing work across agent teams. Both are untested suggestions presented as lessons.

The structured 'read the paper and answer these questions' step before /plan (§3.1) was meant to verify comprehension, yet the agent's paraphrase carried the source's omission through. This is a direct observation against relying on explain-back as the comprehension check for P38.
note: I agree with the review's verdict and with its reading of this as a two-case, uncontrolled field report in which the headline 'AGENTS.md reduced hallucination' is unsupported. I lower the source-omission and human-review claim to weak: there is one omission incident, and the paper credits review and testing together, so 'review is needed' is not isolated. I move P16 from neutral to introduces, because the V&V suite is a required CI gate and the agent ran tests. I would add P21 for the pre-commit hook and branch-protection prescription. My blind rigor score was one point lower than the review's, because the only quantitative figure is a calibrated fit.
